name: Andaman & Nicobar
tagline: Port Blair, Havelock & Neil — Coral Reefs, Turquoise Water & White Sand
shortDescription: Three islands, one trip — Port Blair for the history, Havelock for Radhanagar Beach and the diving, Neil for the quiet. Flights, ferries and hotels all book up early, which is the real reason people take a package.
fullOverview: Almost every Andaman trip is the same three islands in the same order: Port Blair, where the flights land and the Cellular Jail is; Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), which has Radhanagar Beach and most of the diving; and Neil (Shaheed Dweep), which is quieter and usually shorter. What makes the planning awkward is not the sightseeing, it is the joins — inter-island ferries run to a fixed timetable, sell out weeks ahead in season, and a missed one costs you a day. That, more than anything, is why most travellers book this as a package rather than assembling it themselves. Five to seven days covers all three without rushing; a shorter trip usually means dropping Neil.
bestTime: October to May is the season — calm seas, reliable ferries and the best underwater visibility for diving and snorkelling | June to September is the monsoon, when sea crossings are rougher and can be cancelled at short notice

howToReach.air: Veer Savarkar International Airport, Port Blair (IXZ), with direct flights from Chennai, Kolkata, Delhi and Bengaluru. Chennai and Kolkata are the shortest hops and usually the cheapest.
howToReach.rail: Not applicable — the Andamans are an island territory with no rail link.
howToReach.road: Travel between islands is by sea, not road. Private catamarans (Makruzz, Nautika) run Port Blair–Havelock–Neil on a fixed daily timetable and sell out weeks ahead in season; local sightseeing on each island is by cab or auto.

topAttractions.name: Radhanagar Beach, Havelock
topAttractions.description: The one everybody comes for — a long curve of white sand backed by forest, and the best sunset on the islands. Busiest between 4pm and dusk.

topAttractions.name: Elephant Beach, Havelock
topAttractions.description: Reached by speedboat, and where most of the water activities happen — Discover Scuba Diving, snorkelling, sea walking. Reef is close in, so you do not need to be a swimmer.

topAttractions.name: Cellular Jail, Port Blair
topAttractions.description: The colonial prison that held India's freedom fighters, now a national memorial. Go for the evening light and sound show rather than only the daytime visit.

topAttractions.name: Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep)
topAttractions.description: Smaller, slower and far less built up than Havelock. Bharatpur and Laxmanpur beaches, the natural rock bridge, and not much else — which is the point.

topAttractions.name: Port Blair town
topAttractions.description: Where you land and usually where the trip ends. The waterfront, the local markets and the museums fill the half-day either side of a flight without needing a plan.

stayCategories.recommendation: Common in Port Blair and inland on Havelock. Check the distance to the beach — inland Havelock is a 10-15 minute drive from Radhanagar and cabs are not always waiting.
What most package travellers end up in on Havelock. Worth confirming whether it is actually beachfront or beach-access, because the listings use both words loosely.
A handful of properties on Havelock and Neil. These are the first to sell out for Christmas, New Year and the April–May holidays — book months ahead.

travelTips: Indian citizens need no passport or special permit for Port Blair, Havelock or Neil — a photo ID is enough.
Book inter-island ferries as early as you book the flights. They run to a fixed timetable, sell out weeks ahead in season, and a missed crossing costs you a whole day.
Compare packages on what is included, not on the headline price. Ferry class, airport transfers and whether water activities are covered change the real cost more than the hotel does.
Water activities at Elephant Beach are usually paid to the operators on the spot. Agree the rate before you start, and ask what is included — photos and video are often charged separately.
Sea conditions decide diving and snorkelling, not the calendar. Keep a spare day if the underwater activities are the reason you are going.
Mobile signal is patchy on Havelock and Neil, and data is slow. Download your tickets and maps before you leave Port Blair.
Book early for Christmas, New Year and the April–May school holidays — these are the most expensive and most crowded weeks of the year.

faqs.question: How many days are enough for an Andaman trip?
faqs.answer: Five to seven days covers Port Blair, Havelock and Neil without rushing, which is why our packages are built that way. A shorter trip usually means dropping Neil — the islands are joined by scheduled ferries, so each move costs you most of a morning and you cannot compress that.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Andaman?
faqs.answer: October to May. The sea is calm, the ferries run reliably and underwater visibility is at its best for diving and snorkelling. June to September is the monsoon: it is cheaper and much quieter, but crossings get rough and can be cancelled at short notice, which is a real risk on a fixed itinerary.

faqs.question: What does an Andaman tour package cost?
faqs.answer: Our 6-day Andaman package starts at ₹22,999 per person on twin sharing, plus 5% GST, covering hotels, island transfers, ferry tickets and sightseeing. Flights to Port Blair are quoted separately because the fare swings more than the rest of the trip combined. The final figure moves with your dates, hotel category and group size — Christmas, New Year and the April–May holidays are the dearest weeks.

faqs.question: Do we need to know swimming for scuba diving in Andaman?
faqs.answer: No. Discover Scuba Diving is run one-to-one with a certified divemaster and needs no swimming ability or prior certification. If you would still rather stay on the surface, snorkelling at Elephant Beach shows you much of the same reef.

faqs.question: Do Indian citizens need a permit for Andaman?
faqs.answer: Not for Port Blair, Havelock or Neil — a government photo ID is enough. Some of the outer and tribal-reserve islands are restricted and are not part of any standard itinerary, ours included.

faqs.question: Is Andaman good for a family trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is easier than it looks. The beaches are calm, Discover Scuba works for most ages, and the travelling is by boat and short cab rides rather than long drives. The part worth planning around is the ferry timings — with small children or elderly parents, tell us and we will book the shorter crossings and leave more room between them.

faqs.question: How do you travel between the islands?
faqs.answer: By sea. Private catamarans — Makruzz and Nautika — run Port Blair to Havelock to Neil on a fixed daily timetable and take roughly 1 to 2 hours a leg. Government ferries are cheaper and slower. We book the private ones as part of the package because they are the ones that keep an itinerary on schedule.

faqs.question: Can an Andaman package be customised?
faqs.answer: Yes. Nights per island, hotel category, ferry class and which activities are included are all adjustable, and we can quote with or without flights. Tell us your dates, headcount and budget and you will get an itemised quote rather than a fixed menu.
